passage: Imran, it's Kashish. Before your first flu season here, let me tell you about mine. Last year I came into the office with a fever because I didn't want the team to think I was unreliable. New job, big client, you know. I sat there sweating, drinking tea after tea, and sent the client a report with last quarter's figures. Twice. Then I snapped at our manager when she asked if I was okay. By Friday, three people on our floor were ill, including an intern who had just started. So what did I actually prove? That I was reliable at spreading germs. This year, when I felt it coming on, I messaged the team: "Unwell, resting today, here's where my files are." Nobody minded. The work waited. That's the more responsible choice, honestly.

qa.q: What did Kashish send the client by mistake?
qa.a: A report with last quarter's figures, twice.

qa.q: Why did Kashish come in with a fever last year?
qa.a: Kashish was afraid of seeming unreliable in a new job with a big client.

qa.q: What did Kashish do differently this year, and why was it better?
qa.a: Kashish messaged the team, rested and shared where the files were, which protected colleagues and avoided mistakes.

qa.q: How were Kashish's colleagues affected by last year's choice?
qa.a: Three people on the floor fell ill, including a new intern, and the manager got snapped at for asking kindly.

grounding: Shows a young professional working with a fever out of fear of seeming unreliable, making mistakes and spreading illness, then choosing to rest and tell the team.

passage: I'm Lokesh, and I sit across from Sarika in accounts. On Monday she came in wrapped in a shawl, eyes watery, sneezing into tissue after tissue. When I asked, she said, "Just a cold. I can't miss audit week." By noon she had entered two invoices in the wrong month; I caught one of them. She kept saying sorry. I couldn't tell if she felt more ill or more scared. Our team lead, Farida, walked over, looked at her and said, "Home. Rest. Tell me what's urgent and I'll share it out." Sarika looked close to tears, relieved or embarrassed, I'm not sure. By Thursday two more of us were sniffling anyway. She came back the next week, much brighter, and caught a mistake of mine.

qa.q: What was Sarika wrapped in on Monday?
qa.a: A shawl.

qa.q: What might Sarika have been worried about by coming in?
qa.a: She was worried about missing audit week and letting the team down, perhaps scared of seeming unreliable.

qa.q: What did Farida's response get right?
qa.a: Sending Sarika home to rest and sharing out the urgent work, which protected both Sarika and the team from mistakes and illness.

qa.q: How does Lokesh see Sarika's choice to work?
qa.a: Lokesh notices the errors and the illness spreading, but cannot tell whether Sarika felt more ill or more scared.

grounding: Illustrates a young professional pushing on while unwell, making mistakes and spreading illness, and resting as the more responsible choice.

passage:
"Zubin, you sound terrible."
"I'm fine, Vandana. Just a cold."
"You've sneezed eleven times this meeting. And you sent the client the draft with last year's figures."
"Oh no. Seriously?"
"Seriously. I caught it. Why are you here with a fever?"
"Because I'm new. If I take leave in my second month, you'll think I'm unreliable."
"What I'll think is that you gave half the team your flu. Priya's already coughing."
"I didn't think about that."
"Go home. Rest. Message the team that you're off sick, and I'll move your deadlines."
"You won't mark it against me?"
"Going home is the responsible move. Staying and making mistakes is the risky one."
"Okay. Going. Thank you."

qa.q: What did Zubin send the client?
qa.a: The draft with last year's figures.

qa.q: Why did Zubin come to work with a fever?
qa.a: Zubin was afraid of seeming unreliable as a new employee in the second month.

qa.q: What made going home the responsible choice?
qa.a: Staying led to mistakes and spread illness to colleagues, while resting and telling the team protects both the work and the people.

qa.q: How does Vandana see Zubin pushing on?
qa.a: Vandana sees it as risky, causing errors and a coughing colleague, not as dedication.

grounding: Shows a young professional working with a fever out of fear of seeming unreliable, making mistakes and spreading illness, and being told rest is responsible.

passage: Last monsoon I went to work with a fever three days running, because I'd only been at the design studio for four months and was scared of looking flaky. I'm Shalini. I wrapped a scarf round my face, drank chai by the flask, and kept going. On day three I sent the printer the wrong file for a restaurant menu: two hundred copies. By Friday Sunaina, who sits beside me, was sick too, and so was the intern. My boss didn't shout. She just said, "I'd rather lose you for two days than lose the team for a week." That stung more than shouting. Now when I'm ill, I message the team first thing, hand over what's urgent, and stay home. Nobody has called me unreliable. They did call me a germ factory, once.

qa.q: How many copies of the wrong menu were printed?
qa.a: Two hundred copies.

qa.q: Why did Shalini keep working with a fever?
qa.a: Shalini was scared of looking flaky after only four months at the studio.

qa.q: What does Shalini do now when ill?
qa.a: Messages the team first thing, hands over what's urgent, and stays home.

qa.q: How might Sunaina feel about catching the fever?
qa.a: Sunaina was probably annoyed and unwell, paying for Shalini's choice to come in sick.

grounding: Shows a young professional who pushed on with a fever from fear of seeming unreliable, made a costly mistake and spread illness, then learned to rest and tell the team.

passage:
Supervisor's note, Wednesday
Arnab came in feverish again today, second day running, flushed and coughing into his sleeve. He missed a line in the safety checklist that I had to correct, and he snapped at Priyanka when she asked him to repeat a reading. When I asked him to go home, he said, "I don't want you to think I'm unreliable. I've only just been made permanent." I told him that being reliable includes telling us when he is sick, so we can plan, and that working ill puts both the checks and the team at risk. He left at noon. I've asked the team to cover his readings until he's well and told HR there is no mark against him.
Vishal

qa.q: What did Arnab miss?
qa.a: A line in the safety checklist.

qa.q: What was Arnab afraid of?
qa.a: He was afraid of being seen as unreliable, having only just been made permanent.

qa.q: Why was Vishal's response responsible?
qa.a: Vishal sent Arnab home, arranged cover and made clear there would be no mark, protecting the safety checks, the team and Arnab's health.

qa.q: How might Priyanka have felt when Arnab snapped at her?
qa.a: Priyanka was likely taken aback and a bit hurt, since she had only asked him to repeat a reading.

grounding: Shows a young professional working with a fever from fear of seeming unreliable, making mistakes, and being sent home as the responsible choice.

passage:
Tuesday, 11 pm
Stupid, stupid day. Woke up with a fever and a scratchy throat but went in anyway, because missing the sprint review would make me look unreliable. By noon I'd pasted the wrong figures into the client deck and had to redo half of it. Reena covered for me in the meeting, then pulled me aside. 'You're burning up. And half the floor will catch this now.' She was right; Kunal was already sneezing. The manager sent me home at two. I felt ashamed, not of being ill, but of pretending I wasn't. Tomorrow I'm staying home, and I've already messaged the team. If the fever keeps going, I'll see the doctor.
Yogesh

qa.q: What mistake did Yogesh make by noon?
qa.a: Pasted the wrong figures into the client deck.

qa.q: Why did Yogesh go to work with a fever?
qa.a: Yogesh was afraid that missing the sprint review would look unreliable.

qa.q: What is Yogesh doing differently tomorrow?
qa.a: Staying home, having already told the team, and seeing the doctor if the fever keeps going.

qa.q: How might Reena have felt watching Yogesh work while ill?
qa.a: Reena was probably worried and a bit annoyed, covering in the meeting and seeing colleagues at risk of catching it.

grounding: A young professional works with a fever out of fear of seeming unreliable, makes mistakes and spreads illness, then chooses rest.
